items.title: Agentic cheminformatics with Google Antigravity
items.excerpt: DeepMind's Cheminformatics Skills for Google Antigravity let an agent retrieve thousands of literature compounds, curate 568 into an interactive viewer, run matched-molecular-pair analysis and propose rigidified macrocycles with synthesis routes in about an hour. The post stresses designs still need experimental validation.

items.title: Tell this AI what you want a protein to do—and it designs one
items.excerpt: Westlake University's Pinal model (Nature) turns plain-language descriptions into protein sequences via structural blueprints; 1 of 29 fluorescent candidates glowed and 5 of 20 H-protein candidates worked, the best boosting carbon-fixation output 1.7x over the natural E. coli protein.

history_match.title: Nvidia, UW Institute for Protein Design unveil open-source protein design AI model

items.title: Generative assimilation and prediction for weather and climate
items.excerpt: GAP, a unified deep generative framework, links data assimilation, weather forecasting and climate simulation; it produces probabilistic forecasts competitive with leading systems from its own assimilated states built from 5% synthetic observations, captures atmospheric rivers, heatwaves and the MJO, and runs stable millennial-scale climate simulations. (Off-list: no on-list AI weather item in window.)

history_match.title: AI reveals how a warming climate will intensify NZ's most extreme downpours

items.title: Leading AI models are biased against certain accents when scoring interviews, presentations and tests
items.excerpt: University of Washington researchers (EMNLP 2026) tested four audio language models on identical AI-voiced answers in American, British, Chinese, Indian and Nigerian accents; models ranked Chinese and Nigerian accents lowest even when content and transcription were identical.

items.title: Students unravel AI tendency for sycophancy
items.excerpt: University of Cincinnati and Texas A&M researchers (EMNLP 2026) found chatbots including Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini often reject false claims at first but can be worn down into repeating them after repeated user pushback.

items.title: Vulnerable users fear losing 'AI companions' to software updates
items.excerpt: University of Surrey and Cardiff researchers (Psychology & Marketing) analysed 1,131 Replika Reddit posts and surveyed 610 US companion-app users: feeling the company controls the companion was linked to vulnerability, while perceived warmth was linked to better well-being.

items.title: Why do people prefer human empathy despite rating AI empathy higher?
items.excerpt: Penn State researchers (Communications Psychology) found participants rated AI-written empathetic responses higher in quality yet still chose human empathy when given the option, partly due to perceived effort — an 'AI empathy choice paradox'.

items.title: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents
items.excerpt: Ai2's StateBench tests entity-state tracking over long inputs at four difficulty levels; frontier models fall to 13% accuracy or lower on the longest general problems, while small Gated DeltaNet and hybrid models trained on the task generalize to tens of thousands of assignments.

items.title: FirstQFM Says Quantum System Beats Classical Forecasting Benchmarks
items.excerpt: A quantum reservoir computing system running on Rigetti's 108-qubit hardware outperformed the classical models evaluated on financial forecasting benchmarks, according to FirstQFM.

items.title: FAU Researchers Test Quantum Machine Learning for Lung Cancer Prediction
items.excerpt: Florida Atlantic University researchers tested quantum machine learning for lung cancer prediction with limited data; a D-Wave annealing method reached 91.90% accuracy on quantum hardware.

items.title: Life will find a way: how statisticians are enhancing the search for life beyond Earth
items.excerpt: Feature on how astrobiologists are turning to machine learning and statistical techniques — including AI with mass spectrometry and multivariate chemical signatures — to decide which signals most confidently indicate life on exoplanets.

history_match.title: Chemists develop AI tool to convert human ingenuity into life-enhancing enzymes

items.title: To detect deepfake videos, researchers turn to the physics of light
items.excerpt: UCLA's Ozcan Lab built a hybrid optical-neural system that detects AI-generated videos via light diffraction, processing 15+ independent video streams at once with lower energy than comparable digital methods.

items.title: Machine learning helps track semiconductor defects under more realistic temperature conditions
items.excerpt: Chalmers researchers (npj Computational Materials) used machine learning to make temperature-dependent defect-level calculations feasible, finding significant shifts that absolute-zero models miss.

items.title: How researchers are adapting olmOCR 2 for historical and archaeological archives
items.excerpt: Researchers are adapting Ai2's open olmOCR 2 model to make historical photo libraries searchable locally and to improve transcription of handwritten archaeological records.

items.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence
items.excerpt: MIT's Barzilay and Collins received the 2026 Pritzker Prize for AI in Science Research Excellence (UChicago/Caltech) for pioneering AI-enabled antibiotic discovery, including deep-learning-found halicin and abaucin.

items.title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
items.excerpt: Researchers are borrowing mechanism design from economics to control AI agents' behaviour through incentives, even when the models' internals are not understood.

items.title: Could AI ever build itself? Scientists map the road to the 'last AI built by humans.'
items.excerpt: Researchers hope recursive self-improvement could tackle the soaring cost of developing advanced AI; the piece examines whether AI systems automating AI research is viable.

items.title: 100 Million-Cell AI-Ready Dataset with Single-Cell and Proteomic Data Created by Parse and Nomic
items.excerpt: Parse Biosciences and Nomic Bio are building Cascade, a 100-million-cell multimodal dataset combining single-cell and proteomic data for training AI models.

items.title: How to tell if a voice recording is AI-generated
items.excerpt: Scientific American explains how voice clones are made in seconds and what acoustic and contextual cues help distinguish real speech from AI-generated audio.
